correctness.rationale: For any 3×3 matrix with unit-modulus entries, normalize first row/column to 1. If (u-1)(t-1)=(v-1)(w-1)≠0, conjugation and unimodularity imply ut=vw and u+t=v+w, hence equal two-element multisets and a repeated row or column; zero-product cases likewise produce a proportional pair. For characters on Z3×Zp, proportional rows occur exactly when their difference has order 3 or p and the three columns lie in its annihilator coset, yielding four pure/collision configurations including transposes. Rank one needs entire selected row space to be proportional and forces complementary 3-pure/p-pure sets. Count 3-pure row triples as 3*binom(p,3), p-pure as p; p-colliding as p+9p(p-1), 3-colliding as T-p³, subtract precisely the two 3pure/p-pure overlaps. This gives N1,N2,N3 as stated for all primes. Independently enumerated every possible triple-pair incidence for p=5 and p=7: (300,13800,192925) and (1470,91728,1675702). Those finite checks do not prove complex-character rigidity for all primes; the general proof does.
